senses.sense_definition: The everyday language or dialect spoken by ordinary people in a particular region.

examples.text: The author wrote the novel in the local <w>vernacular</w> to capture the authentic voice of the characters.
It is often difficult for foreigners to understand the <w>vernacular</w> used in casual street conversations.

senses.sense_definition: The native language or national language of a specific country or people.

examples.text: After centuries of colonial rule, the country finally promoted its own <w>vernacular</w> in schools and government.
The poet chose to write in the <w>vernacular</w> rather than the formal language used by the elite.

senses.sense_definition: A style of architecture that uses local materials and traditional building methods.

examples.text: The village is famous for its traditional <w>vernacular</w> that blends perfectly with the surrounding landscape.
Modern architects are increasingly looking to the <w>vernacular</w> for inspiration on sustainable building practices.

senses.sense_definition: Relating to the everyday language used by ordinary people, rather than formal or scientific speech.

examples.text: The professor explained the complex theory using <w>vernacular</w> terms so that everyone could understand.
He preferred using <w>vernacular</w> expressions instead of the stiff and formal language of the courtroom.

senses.sense_definition: Referring to a common name for a plant or animal, as opposed to its scientific Latin name.

examples.text: While the scientific name is complex, the <w>vernacular</w> name for this flower is simply buttercup.
Field guides often list both the scientific classification and the <w>vernacular</w> name for easy identification.
